newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Intel sees Asia sales flat to slightly up.
newsitem.headline: Intel sees Asia sales flat to slightly up.

text.p: Computer chip maker Intel Corp said on Thursday it saw flat to slightly higher revenues from Asia on a quarterly basis through the rest of 1997.

"We've had a huge surge in the last six to nine months. Looking out for the next three months, some of those (Asian markets) are going to slightly quieter periods, some are slightly livelier periods. The underlying PC growth across Asia is strong, the net result will be flat to slightly up," Paul Otellini, Intel's executive vice president and director of sales and marketing told a news conference.
He said this pattern of growth could continue over the course of the year.
Intel earlier this week announced better-than-expected first quarter results with net profit of US$1.98 billion on revenues of US$6.45 billion.
It also said it expected its global revenues to be flat to slightly higher in the second quarter compared to the first quarter.
Sean Maloney, vice president and general manager of Asia Pacific operations, said Intel would double investment in Asia over the next 18 to 24 months in its assembly and test operations.
Company officials were not immediately able to give an investment figure.
Intel had announced during the release of its first quarter results it was planning US$4.5 billion in capital expenditure in 1997.
Maloney said more of Intel's expenditure was being spent on assembly and test operations in Asia, besides being used to expand its wafer fabrication plants in the U.S., Mexico and Ireland.
Intel has assembly and tests plants in China, Malaysia and Philippines.
